## 開篇固定收益論點

8月13日美國公債收盤全面上漲，但各期限表現清楚顯示：聯準會可以耐心觀望，不代表長期財政壓力已經緩解。2年期殖利率下跌5個基點至4.15%，5年期下跌6個基點至4.32%，10年期下跌5個基點至4.63%，30年期則僅回落3個基點至5.21%。2年期與10年期利差持平於48個基點，2年期與30年期利差則擴大2個基點至106個基點。市場降低再次升息的急迫性，卻未消除長天期供給所附帶的溢價。

7月生產者物價是當日最關鍵的變化。整體PPI與6月持平，年增率由5.5%降至4.7%，減速幅度大於預期。核心生產者物價月增0.2%，年增4.2%。能源價格下跌3.1%，為連續第2個月下滑；食品價格創年初以來最大跌幅；運輸與倉儲成本下跌1.8%，為2023年4月以來最大降幅。結合前一日溫和的CPI及7月招聘轉弱，這份數據顯示，戰爭引發的價格衝擊在美國實際數據中並未如原先擔心般持久。

利率拆解支持上述解讀，但尚不足以宣告通膨風險已經結束。10年期實質殖利率下跌3個基點至2.39%，10年期損益兩平通膨率下跌2個基點至2.24%；成長調整後的折現率與通膨補償同步促成名目公債上漲。貨幣市場將9月升息的隱含機率降至40%以下，2年期殖利率也率先回吐前一週對政策路徑的重定價。然而即使經過本輪上漲，30年期殖利率在1個月內仍上升11個基點，相較之下，2年期與5年期分別下跌11個及5個基點。

規模$250億的30年期公債標售，解釋了部分期限差異。得標殖利率為5.216%，較標售前殖利率高不到0.5個基點，並創2001年以來最高得標利率。投標倍數為2.39，接近前6次同類標售的2.36平均值。需求尚稱充足，長債價格收盤仍上漲，但政府必須付出歷史高檔的借款利率才能完成發行。週四近期標售風險順利落幕，未出現失序尾差；同時也確認，投資人只願在絕對殖利率偏高時承接存續期間。

風險資產將通膨結果視為政策喘息，而非衰退訊號。標普500指數上漲0.65%至歷史新高，那斯達克 100上漲1.15%；WTI下跌2.33%至$81.33，Brent下跌2.10%至$87.11。LQD上漲0.41%、HYG上漲0.23%、JNK上漲0.20%、EMB上漲0.44%。這些基金報酬同時包含利率與風險效果，不能證明現券利差收斂，但顯示美國公債上漲時，信用市場仍正常運作、成長型資產同步走強，並非資金逃離風險。

整體平穩的收盤，掩蓋長期資本競爭日益升高。AMD完成史上最大筆美元債發行，募得$47.5億；一筆$22.5億、評等Ba2的資料中心融資，搭配Jane Street的15年租約；資產負債表已認列負債之外，據報超大型雲端服務商的租賃承諾已達$1兆。同時，Telesat以面臨$21億到期壓力的舊有業務作為基礎借入$1.2億；烏克蘭鐵路仍處於違約，並準備提出另一份重整方案。基準殖利率下跌降低當日折現率，卻未消除生產性產能融資與受損資產負債表再融資之間日益擴大的分野。

## 通膨降溫爭取時間，未帶來共識

生產者物價報告強化了初期能源衝擊正在消退、尚未全面嵌入美國生產鏈的論點。整體年增率4.7%仍遠高於聯準會的2%目標，但較6月下降0.8個百分點，加上月增率持平，已構成明確的方向轉變。能源、食品、貨運與倉儲成本下跌，顯示先前將伊朗戰爭衝擊傳導至消費者與企業價格的管道正在降溫。週四原油下跌也提供同日市場訊號，表明短期價格動能確實消退，而非僅被基期效應掩蓋。

細項並非全面降溫。電子零組件與配件價格較1年前上漲近28%，接近歷史最快增速；電腦與電腦設備價格更創下9.8%的紀錄漲幅。這些類別呼應前一日CPI呈現的科技相關商品通膨，並將AI資本支出熱潮連結至明確的成本管道。投資組合管理費創1年多來最大漲幅，醫院門診照護費用也大幅上升。相對而言，醫師服務與住院照護價格溫和，機票價格大跌，貿易服務利潤率也在6月上升後回落，因此價格廣度呈現分歧，而非普遍加速。

上述價格組成將直接影響聯準會偏好的通膨指標。花旗、摩根士丹利與傑富瑞的經濟學家在檢視PPI細項後，預估7月核心PCE月增0.2%。若數據符合這項預估，配合先前弱於預期的就業報告，仍可為9月按兵不動保留一條狹窄路徑，但不足以證明通膨已回到目標。美國對多數主要貿易夥伴進口商品課徵至少10%關稅，加上科技投入品價格居高不下，仍可能向下游轉嫁；就業放緩則讓決策官員有理由繼續觀察，而非預先承諾政策方向。

克里夫蘭聯準銀行總裁Beth Hammack最明確反對市場的結論。她週四在俄亥俄州表示，近期通膨走低令人欣慰，卻不足以讓她相信通膨會持續放緩至2%。她重申目前利率並未形成實質限制，主張現在就必須採取行動，並維持其7月反對按兵不動時所支持的升息25個基點立場。她的論點並非最新數據重新加速，而是在通膨水準仍高、當前政策立場可能不足以壓抑需求之際，一連串有利數據仍不足以形成信心。

因此，政策陣營的共識程度不如9月升息機率低於40%所暗示。里奇蒙聯準銀行總裁Tom Barkin提出相反的短期論點：通膨下降支持利率持平，但根深蒂固的價格壓力最終仍可能要求緊縮。前達拉斯聯準銀行總裁Robert Kaplan同樣支持7月按兵不動，並主張在9月前保持開放態度，因為AI投資、關稅、勞動力限制與油價會推升通膨，AI應用及中國產能過剩則會壓低通膨。Kaplan目前身為高盛副董事長，而非現任決策官員；他的觀點可充實市場辯論，卻不代表新增一票。

美國公債殖利率曲線有效反映這項張力。2年期殖利率下跌5個基點，重定價近期政策決策；5年期下跌6個基點，則反映預期緊縮路徑降低。30年期漲幅較小，顯示下次會議保持耐心，不等於市場已對通膨終點建立信心。10年期實質殖利率仍為2.39%，過去1個月上升3個基點；30年期實質殖利率仍為2.97%，同期上升8個基點。通膨補償下降有利週四債市，但實質資本成本依然處於歷史上嚴苛的水準。

跨資產表現進一步凸顯政策利多的侷限。股市創下新高，超大型雲端服務商支出重燃科技股熱情，帶動那斯達克表現優於大盤；但VIX不降反升0.55%至14.63，未確認波動率全面崩跌。美元指數僅下跌0.09%至99.921。黃金期貨收盤近乎持平於$4,415.60，儘管稍後現貨交易顯示週四跌至$4,400以下。跨資產走勢顯示聯準會近期壓力降低、地緣政治與機構避險需求持續的情境，而非單一總體因素主導所有市場。

## 高利率仍能為長天期公債找到買盤

30年期公債標售既非失敗，也不能證明財政溢價已經消失。5.216%的得標殖利率略高於發行前參考殖利率，顯示需求稍遜於標售前預期，但落差不到0.5個基點，投標倍數也大致正常。30年期殖利率當日收盤約下跌3個基點，標售前一度跌得更多。投資人消化既定供給，並保留部分通膨帶動的漲幅；代價則是承接近25年來最高的標售殖利率。

前一日10年期公債標售的結果，讓訊號更加清楚。規模$420億的10年期公債得標殖利率為4.683%，是2007年以來最高融資成本；隔日長債標售又以5.216%完成。兩次標售在異常高的殖利率下仍獲得足額投標，表示市場准入並非問題。真正問題在於，持續赤字、通膨前景不明，以及聯準會與海外官方機構的結構性支持減少之際，對價格敏感的民間投資人承接更大債務存量時，政府必須付出何種市場出清價格。

惠譽週四維持美國AA+評等，但警告減稅與關稅退稅將使2026年財政赤字占GDP比重擴大。本會計年度迄今，公共債務利息支出達$1.17兆，較1年前增加15%，部分原因正是美國公債殖利率上升。利率與利息支出的回饋循環，使長期殖利率既是市場價格，也是財政成本的投入變數。30年期房貸利率升至6.69%，創2025年7月以來最高，也顯示相同基準利率正傳導至家庭融資。

美國財政部近期措辭由考慮未來附息債標售規模「增加」，改為考慮「變動」，因而開啟縮減長債標售規模的可能性，但目前尚未實際減量。若將更多發行轉往2年至7年期公債，確實可以降低最長端釋出的存續期間，卻只是把再融資與政策路徑曝險移至較短期限，而非縮小借款需求。Kaplan認為長期殖利率反映全球結構性供需失衡，而非聯邦資金利率；全球供需失衡的疑慮正說明，9月按兵不動無法單獨修復殖利率曲線。

現券市場活動證實，週四債市上漲與標售期間的成交相當活躍。名目附息債以原始面額計算的成交量達$9,921億，較前一交易日增加4.9%。7年至10年期區間成交量增加25.8%至$2,303億，20年期以上成交量增加34.3%至$1,131億；交易商對客戶交易占比分別為46.7%與49.3%。這些數字顯示雙向風險移轉活躍，而非投資人的方向性，並使收盤期限結構比清淡交易日更具資訊價值。

資金市場並未放大存續期間事件。聯準會表示，在截至9月14日的每月期間內，不會為準備金管理而買進國庫券，但仍計畫進行約$170億的再投資購買。8月12日SOFR定盤利率為3.62%，較準備金餘額利率低3個基點；8月5日銀行準備金為$3兆，高於年底的$2.85兆。即使國庫券發行增加，相較於擔保品，現金仍相當充裕，使聯準會得以暫停購買，而不致釋放重啟量化緊縮的訊號。

暫停購買是對準備金充裕程度的技術性判斷，並非貨幣政策改變。準備金管理購買於2025年12月以每月近$400億開始，4月降至$250億、5月降至$100億，接著在即將到來的期間停止。因此，前端同時包含兩項不同訊息：通膨降溫壓低預期政策利率，貨幣市場環境寬鬆則降低增加準備金的必要。兩者都不代表融資壓力。區分政策利率與準備金需求後，長端溢價仍聚焦於存續期間、赤字與通膨不確定性，而非眼前的流動性短缺。

## AI融資從題材轉為負債

AMD發行$47.5億債券，使AI投資週期轉化為實際的投資等級債供給。這家晶片製造商發行4個券次，期限介於3年至10年；最長券次的定價由初步討論水準收緊約25個基點，最終為美國公債加90個基點。募集資金可用於償債或一般企業用途，包括下月到期的$8.75億債券。穩健的資產負債表支持本次發行：截至6月27日，AMD債務為$32億，現金及短期投資則有$131億。

這次發債仍擴大AI周邊的資本承諾。AMD已同意對Anthropic投資最多$50億；分析師估計，隨著與Anthropic及Microsoft的協議擴大晶片需求，2026年營收將成長47%，超過$510億。定價較初步討論收緊，顯示投資人接受這筆4券次交易僅提供溫和的新券讓利。這也讓另一家大型借款人加入同一資金池，與資料中心、公用事業、設備及政府赤字共同競逐資本。

Zenith Arc說明這類需求如何移向專案信用。Fluidstack與Next Frontier在奧克拉荷馬州合資的資料中心專案，發行$22.5億、5年期優先擔保綠色債券，穆迪評等為Ba2。募集資金用於興建運算設施與變電站，支援約149兆瓦。Jane Street一家子公司簽署15年絕對三重淨租賃，除基本租金外，承租人還須負擔營運成本、稅負、公用事業費、保險與電力費用，並由Jane Street Group提供慣常保證。租約將重要營運義務轉由財力雄厚的承租人承擔，但專案本身仍低於投資等級。

這筆交易有別於Jane Street自身在前一交易日完成的$146億擔保債發行。兩者合併觀察，顯示這家造市商既是企業借款人，也是另一筆基礎建設債務的合約收入支柱。Edged Compute今年已發行$13億綠色債券，TeraWulf也為資料中心取得$32億融資。這類專案的永續發行量由2024年的$76億增至2025年的$112億。綠色標籤可擴大潛在投資人基礎，卻不會消除施工、電力、技術或承租人集中風險。

較不顯眼的負債，規模比目前債券發行日程所顯示的更大。由Amanda Lynam領導的高盛信用分析師團隊估計，超大型雲端服務商已認列的租賃承諾約為$2,000億，財務報表附註另揭露$1兆尚未起租的租約，後者在不到1個月內由$7,250億上升。這些合約要到付款及使用開始後才會列為租賃負債，但已代表對未來現金流的請求權，以及一批在啟用前需要建設融資的設施。

資本競爭已經影響信用市場的優質端。法國巴黎銀行發現，LVMH、Sanofi及BAE Systems等高品質歐洲企業的CDS，自年底以來上升超過10%，儘管這些發行人並未直接參與資料中心。全球投資等級債利差約為80個基點，僅比今年稍早創下的金融危機後低點高約6個基點。超大型雲端服務商大規模發債時，低利差企業必須與規模更大、流動性更佳的替代標的競爭；即使自身營運未惡化，風險定價也可能向指數水準靠攏。

週四整體信用債報酬維持有序。LQD上漲0.41%，高於高收益債基金約0.20%至0.23%的漲幅，符合投資等級債受惠於更強存續期間行情的表現。補充觀察的長天期公司債指數上漲約0.64%至0.66%，接近長天期美國公債指數0.61%的漲幅。這些總報酬主要反映基準殖利率下降，無法辨識現券利差方向；初級市場定價與發行人條款更能說明資本仍可取得，但競爭日益激烈。

在信用較弱的一端，取得融資並不能解決負債期限錯配。Telesat取得$1.2億定期貸款作為一般企業用途，其舊有地球同步衛星業務則回報營收下降25%、營業虧損C$1,270萬。未來14個月內，公司有4筆、合計約$21億債務到期：$13.2億定期貸款與$3.87億優先擔保票據於12月到期，之後是明年6月到期的$2.25億擔保票據，以及2027年10月到期的$2.13億無擔保票據。公司表示，目前現金流與準備金不足以支付這些債務。

Telesat的公司架構決定回收風險。去年的重組以Telesat GEO而非新的低軌衛星業務作為私人貸款擔保，因而引發仍在進行的債權人訴訟。管理層預期處理到期債務，並維持GEO持續經營，但申報文件對12月債務能否履行提出重大疑慮。一份最長15年、含選擇權價值最高C$27億的加拿大軍方合約，以及符合資格取得美國頻譜重新配置所提供的$1.89億，可支撐整體企業，卻無法單獨支應舊有業務近期到期債務。股價週四下跌13.4%。

烏克蘭鐵路面臨另一種重整難題：已落實的營收措施改善了條件，卻未恢復債權人經濟利益。公司要求調漲45%後，30%的貨運費率漲幅已於8月初生效。這家國營營運商正為$11億債券準備另一份方案，先前協商已於4月破局。公司1月起停止支付利息，約$7億債券已於上月到期但未償還，其餘債務於2028年到期。擬於2027年1月再調漲15%的方案尚未獲准。

先前方案考慮減記20%本金、納入貨運量調整機制、展期至2033年、分期攤還，並隨時間提高票息。提高貨運費率可改善重啟協商的現金流基礎，但戰爭破壞、維修支出、能源與勞動成本、貨運量下降，以及結構性虧損的客運業務仍然存在。正式談判尚未重啟。因此，真正的變化是營運投入條件改善，而非重整完成或付款紀錄恢復。

## 全球緊縮日益在地化

日本對美國公債上漲構成最明顯的海外存續期間挑戰。據報首相Sanae Takaichi領導的政府支持日本央行近期升息，可能時點為9月或10月；日圓疲弱，加上美日協調干預的效果消退，使財政與貨幣當局立場趨於一致。1%的政策利率仍遠低於聯準會的3.5%至3.75%區間。交易員估計日本央行9月18日會議升息機率為74%，日本10年期殖利率微升至2.87%，接近上月創下的30年高點。

最新生產者物價數據強化國內升息理由。日本7月企業商品價格較1年前上漲7.2%，僅略低於6月上修後的7.3%；月增0.1%，6月月增率則上修至0.5%。石油、煤炭、化學品與非鐵金屬是年度價格壓力主因。投入成本壓力使上半年與通膨相關的企業破產達556件，創2018年開始統計以來最高，7月再以121件創單月紀錄。日圓疲弱、能源及AI相關機械需求都推升這項壓力。

匯率反應顯示，一次預期升息不足以化解利差。政府釋放訊號後，日圓一度走強，但收盤為1美元兌159.50日圓，是7月30日以來最弱收盤，並接近過去曾引發干預的160區域。市場焦點已從日本央行是否於9月升息，轉向其後的升息速度。加快正常化可能支撐日圓並留住國內資本，卻也可能壓抑經濟；日本家庭支出截至6月已連續第7個月下滑。

挪威展現較為平衡的按兵不動。挪威央行連續第2次會議將存款利率維持在4.25%，符合受訪16位分析師的一致預期，且未公布新預測。總裁Ida Wolden Bache表示，在2次溫和的核心通膨數據後，委員會需要更多時間，目前仍太早斷定前景已有實質改變。官員仍將薪資成長與緊俏勞動市場視為通膨持續來源，因此仍可能再次升息。交換市場定價反映9月前升息12個基點、年底前升息22個基點，低於前一日的15個與27個基點。

土耳其央行則因不同原因維持限制性立場。總裁Fatih Karahan將年底通膨預測由26%調高至28%，更接近市場調查的29%，並承認先前預測部分未能實現。7月通膨降至31.8%，但能源不確定性使央行仍以40%的隔夜利率提供資金，而非已暫停使用的37%1週期附買回利率。正式2026年目標仍為24%，新的2027年預測與目標均為15%。是否恢復1週期附買回融資，取決於未來市場狀況。

越南顯示成長企圖可能如何碰上銀行體系的融資能力。根據越南國家銀行資料，越南盾貸款比存款高出約2,000兆越南盾，折合$768億。政府力拚下半年近12%成長，並敦促銀行降低放款利率，包括對相同期限提供至少比銀行平均利率低1個百分點的優惠方案。央行同時警告，流動性、國內利率、匯率及金融穩定因素，使貨幣政策支援空間非常有限。

限制同時反映在批發融資與通膨。銀行尋求境外資源之際，Techcombank啟動$10億聯貸；越南國家銀行今年信用成長目標約為15%。7月CPI年增4.45%；若要將2026年平均通膨維持在約4.5%，至年底前每月平均漲幅只能約為0.34%。因此，越南並不具備美國PPI所暗示的明確通膨降溫空間。信用擴張可支持政府成長目標，但存放款缺口已為負值，增加調降管制放款成本轉化為流動性與匯率壓力的風險。

各國政策路徑並不同步。美國數據支持觀望；日本將匯率防衛與提早緊縮相結合；挪威在通膨低於預期後重新評估；土耳其上調預測後維持實質緊縮；越南則在資金缺口下力圖加速信用成長。對固定收益市場而言，共同結果是各地殖利率曲線相互競逐，政策結果分布也更廣。即使美國生產者物價帶動美國公債上漲，當海外投資人在本國面對更具吸引力或更有必要維持的殖利率時，美債長端溢價仍可居高不下。

## 前瞻市場意涵

8月26日公布的7月核心PCE、期間內的就業報告，以及Kevin Warsh在傑克森洞的談話，將決定週四政策敏感天期的漲勢能否延續。若核心PCE接近依生產者物價細項推估的0.2%，招聘持續放緩，且主席願意說明7月按兵不動的理由，將強化9月暫停升息的預期，並使2年至5年期殖利率保持最高敏感度。若服務通膨廣泛、勞動市場證據轉強，或在通膨多年高於目標後更強調政策公信力，則會重新強化Hammack的異議，使前端再次接軌仍偏高的實質利率環境。

實體石油管道仍可能推翻通膨降溫的解讀。若荷姆茲海峽維持通航、貨運與保險摩擦下降，且原油延續週四跌勢，7月能源、食品物流與倉儲價格下跌將成為更持久的通膨投入因素。若攻擊再起、海峽持續封閉或油價再次飆升，這些數據就會成為落後指標，並考驗2年期殖利率與損益兩平通膨率是否再度同步上升。關鍵變化不是另一則談判標題，而是在下一批通膨數據與聯準會決策前，實體流量實際改善或惡化。

日本與印尼將在不同時間尺度提供下一輪海外存續期間考驗。印尼8月14日預算演說必須提出可信、符合3%法定上限的赤字路徑；市場認為低於2.5%的目標及較低淨發行量有利債市，而2.2%的赤字可能使2027年預估淨發行量降至722兆印尼盾，即使總發行量升至1,750兆印尼盾。日本9月18日會議則須顯示，政府支持、7.2%的生產者物價通膨及接近160的日圓，是否足以促成升息及後續路徑指引。印尼維持財政紀律、日本可信落實政策，將支撐當地資產，同時提高美元存續期間面臨的相對價值競爭；若結果令人失望，壓力將轉向兩國貨幣與國內長期殖利率。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

The August 13 Treasury close finally converted softer inflation into a broad rally, yet the maturity pattern preserved the distinction between Federal Reserve patience and long-run fiscal relief. The 2-year yield fell 5 basis points to 4.15%, the 5-year dropped 6 basis points to 4.32%, the 10-year declined 5 basis points to 4.63%, and the 30-year eased only 3 basis points to 5.21%. The 2s10s curve held at 48 basis points, whereas 2s30s steepened 2 basis points to 106. The market reduced the urgency of another increase without removing the premium attached to long-duration supply.

July producer prices delivered the day's decisive change. Headline PPI was unchanged from June and slowed to 4.7% year on year from 5.5%, a larger deceleration than expected. Core producer prices rose 0.2% on the month and 4.2% from a year earlier. Energy fell 3.1%, its second consecutive monthly decline, food posted its largest drop since the start of the year, and transportation and warehousing costs fell 1.8%, the most since April 2023. Combined with the prior day's subdued CPI and weaker July hiring, the release made the war-driven price shock look less persistent in realized U.S. data.

The rates decomposition supports that interpretation but stops short of declaring inflation risk finished. The 10-year real yield fell 3 basis points to 2.39%, and the 10-year breakeven declined 2 basis points to 2.24%. Both growth-adjusted discount rates and inflation compensation contributed to the nominal rally. Money markets reduced the implied chance of a September increase to less than 40%, and the 2-year led the retreat from the prior week's policy path. Even after the rally, however, the 30-year yield remained 11 basis points higher over 1 month, versus declines of 11 basis points at 2 years and 5 basis points at 5 years.

The $25 billion 30-year auction explained part of that asymmetry. It stopped at 5.216%, less than 0.5 basis point above its pre-auction yield and the highest awarded rate since 2001. A 2.39 bid-to-cover ratio was close to the 2.36 average of the previous six comparable sales. Demand was adequate and the long bond still closed higher in price, but clearing required a historically expensive sovereign borrowing rate. Thursday therefore resolved the immediate auction-risk question more favorably than a disorderly tail would have, while confirming that investors will absorb duration only at a high absolute yield.

Risk assets treated the inflation result as a policy reprieve rather than a recession signal. The S&P 500 rose 0.65% to a record and the Nasdaq 100 gained 1.15%, while WTI fell 2.33% to $81.33 and Brent dropped 2.10% to $87.11. LQD gained 0.41%, HYG rose 0.23%, JNK added 0.20%, and EMB advanced 0.44%. Those fund returns combine rates and risk effects and do not establish cash-spread compression, but they show that the Treasury rally coincided with functioning credit and stronger growth assets rather than a flight from risk.

The benign aggregate close conceals a growing contest for long-term capital. AMD raised $4.75 billion in its largest dollar bond sale, a $2.25 billion Ba2 data-center deal came with a 15-year Jane Street lease, and reported hyperscaler lease commitments outside recognized balance-sheet liabilities reached $1 trillion. At the same time, Telesat borrowed $120 million against a legacy business facing $2.1 billion of maturities, and Ukrainian Railways remained in default while preparing another restructuring proposal. Falling benchmark yields eased the day's discount rate; they did not erase the widening divide between financing productive capacity and refinancing impaired balance sheets.

## Disinflation Buys Time, Not Consensus

The producer-price report strengthened the case that the initial energy shock is fading before it becomes embedded across the U.S. production chain. The 4.7% annual headline rate remains far above the Fed's 2% objective, but the 0.8-percentage-point slowdown from June and the flat monthly reading represent a meaningful change in direction. Falling energy, food, freight and warehousing costs connect the moderation to channels that had transmitted the Iran war into consumer and business prices. The decline in crude on Thursday added a same-session market signal that the near-term impulse was receding rather than merely being hidden by base effects.

The details were not uniformly soft. Electronic components and accessories were almost 28% more expensive than a year earlier, near a record pace, and computer and computer-equipment prices rose a record 9.8%. Those categories echo the prior day's CPI evidence of technology-related goods inflation and tie the AI capital boom to a specific cost channel. Portfolio-management fees jumped by the most in more than a year, and hospital outpatient care also increased sharply. Physician services and inpatient hospital care were tame, airfares fell heavily, and trade-service margins retreated after rising in June, leaving breadth mixed rather than broadly accelerating.

That composition matters for the Fed's preferred inflation measure. Citigroup, Morgan Stanley and Jefferies economists projected a 0.2% monthly increase in July core PCE after seeing the PPI components. A result of that size would keep a narrow path open for a September hold, especially alongside the earlier softer-than-expected jobs report. It would not establish that inflation has returned to target. Tariffs of at least 10% on imports from most major trading partners and elevated technology-input prices still create potential pass-through, while the employment slowdown gives policymakers a reason to observe rather than pre-commit.

Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack supplied the clearest resistance to the market's conclusion. Speaking Thursday in Ohio, she said the recent lower inflation readings were welcome but did not give her confidence that inflation would keep slowing sufficiently to reach 2%. She reiterated that rates were not meaningfully restrictive, said action was needed now, and maintained the quarter-point increase she preferred when dissenting against July's hold. Her argument is not that the latest data reaccelerated; it is that one favorable sequence is insufficient when the level of inflation remains high and the current stance may not be restraining demand enough.

The policy coalition is therefore less settled than the less-than-40% September probability implies. Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin has articulated the opposite near-term case: declining inflation supports holding steady, although embedded price pressure could eventually require tightening. Former Dallas Fed President Robert Kaplan likewise endorsed the July hold and urged an open mind through September because AI investment, tariffs, labor constraints and oil pull inflation upward while AI adoption and Chinese overcapacity pull it down. As a Goldman Sachs vice chairman rather than a current policymaker, Kaplan informs the market debate but does not add a vote.

The Treasury curve expressed this tension efficiently. A 5-basis-point decline in the 2-year yield repriced the immediate decision, and the 5-year's 6-basis-point move captured a lower expected path of tightening. The 30-year's smaller rally showed that patience at the next meeting is not equivalent to confidence in the inflation destination. The 10-year real yield remains 2.39%, 3 basis points higher over 1 month, and the 30-year real yield remains 2.97%, 8 basis points higher over the same horizon. Lower inflation compensation helped Thursday, but the real cost of capital stays historically demanding.

Cross assets reinforced the narrowness of the policy relief. Equities reached new highs and the Nasdaq outperformed as hyperscaler spending revived enthusiasm for technology, yet the VIX edged 0.55% higher to 14.63 instead of confirming a wholesale volatility collapse. The Dollar Index slipped only 0.09% to 99.921. Gold futures closed nearly unchanged at $4,415.60 even though later spot trading showed Thursday's decline below $4,400. The combination is compatible with less immediate Fed pressure and persistent geopolitical and institutional hedging, not a single macro factor dominating every market.

## A High Price Still Clears Long Duration

The 30-year auction was neither a failure nor evidence that the fiscal premium has disappeared. Its 5.216% award was slightly above the when-issued reference, so demand fell just short of pre-sale expectations, but the miss was under 0.5 basis point and the bid-to-cover ratio was broadly normal. The 30-year yield finished around 3 basis points lower on the day after rallying more before the auction. Investors absorbed the announced supply and retained part of the inflation-led gain; they did so at the highest auction yield in a quarter century.

The sequence from the prior day's 10-year auction sharpens the message. The $42 billion 10-year sale had stopped at 4.683%, its highest financing cost since 2007. The following long-bond sale then cleared at 5.216%. Two adequately covered auctions at exceptional yields indicate that market access is not the problem. The issue is the sovereign's clearing price as private, price-sensitive investors absorb a larger debt stock amid persistent deficits, uncertain inflation and less structural support from the Fed and foreign official institutions.

Fitch kept the United States at AA+ on Thursday but warned that the fiscal deficit relative to GDP would widen in 2026 because of tax cuts and tariff rebates. Interest expense on the public debt reached $1.17 trillion in the fiscal year to date, 15% more than a year earlier, partly because Treasury yields themselves are higher. That feedback loop turns the long yield into both a market price and a fiscal input. A 30-year mortgage rate of 6.69%, the highest since July 2025, shows the same benchmark transmitting into household financing.

Treasury's recent change in language from considering future coupon-sale "increases" to considering "changes" has opened the possibility of smaller long-bond auctions. No reduction has occurred. Shifting more issuance toward 2- to 7-year notes could reduce the duration delivered at the far end, but it would transfer refinancing and policy-path exposure toward shorter maturities rather than shrink the borrowing requirement. Kaplan's concern that long yields reflect a structural global supply-demand imbalance rather than the fed-funds rate captures why a September hold cannot by itself repair the curve.

Cash-market activity confirms that Thursday's rally and auction occurred amid substantial turnover. Nominal-coupon volume reached $992.1 billion in original-face value, 4.9% above the prior session. Activity in the 7- to 10-year bucket rose 25.8% to $230.3 billion, and volume beyond 20 years increased 34.3% to $113.1 billion. Dealer-to-customer shares were 46.7% and 49.3%, respectively. These figures establish active two-way risk transfer, not investor direction, and make the closing pattern more informative than it would be in a thin session.

Funding markets did not amplify the duration event. The Fed said it would make no reserve-management Treasury-bill purchases in the monthly period ending September 14, although it still plans about $17 billion of reinvestment purchases. SOFR fixed at 3.62% on August 12, 3 basis points below interest on reserve balances, and bank reserves stood at $3 trillion on August 5, up from $2.85 trillion at year-end. Cash has been abundant relative to collateral even as Treasury bill issuance increased, allowing the Fed to pause purchases without signaling a return to quantitative tightening.

The pause is a technical judgment about ample reserves, not a change in monetary policy. Reserve-management purchases began near $40 billion a month in December 2025, fell to $25 billion in April and $10 billion in May, then stopped for the coming period. The front end consequently contains two different messages: softer inflation reduced the expected policy rate, and easy money-market conditions reduced the need for reserve additions. Neither development suggests funding stress. The distinction keeps the long-end premium centered on duration, deficits and inflation uncertainty instead of immediate liquidity scarcity.

## AI Funding Moves From Theme to Liability

AMD's $4.75 billion sale turned the AI investment cycle into realized high-grade supply. The chipmaker issued four tranches from 3 to 10 years, and pricing on the longest maturity tightened by about 25 basis points from initial discussion to 90 basis points over Treasuries. Proceeds may repay debt or fund general corporate purposes, including an $875 million bond maturity next month. The execution was supported by a strong balance sheet: AMD had $3.2 billion of debt against $13.1 billion of cash and short-term investments as of June 27.

The sale still expands the capital committed around AI. AMD has agreed to invest as much as $5 billion in Anthropic, and analyst estimates put 2026 revenue growth at 47% to more than $51 billion as agreements with Anthropic and Microsoft broaden chip demand. Tightening from initial talk shows investors accepted the four-tranche transaction at a modest high-grade concession. It also adds another large borrower to the same capital pool that is financing data centers, utilities, equipment and sovereign deficits.

Zenith Arc illustrates how that demand migrates into project credit. The Oklahoma data-center venture between Fluidstack and Next Frontier offered $2.25 billion of 5-year senior-secured green bonds rated Ba2 by Moody's. Proceeds finance a compute facility and substation supporting about 149 megawatts. A Jane Street subsidiary signed a 15-year absolute triple-net lease, requiring the tenant to cover operating costs, taxes, utilities, insurance and power as well as base rent, with a customary Jane Street Group guaranty. The lease shifts important operating obligations toward a powerful tenant, but the project remains below investment grade.

This transaction is distinct from Jane Street's own $14.6 billion secured sale in the previous session. Together they show the market maker appearing both as a corporate borrower and as the contractual revenue anchor for separate infrastructure debt. Edged Compute had already sold $1.3 billion of green bonds this year and TeraWulf secured $3.2 billion for data centers. Sustainable issuance for such projects reached $11.2 billion in 2025, up from $7.6 billion in 2024. Green designation broadens the potential buyer base but does not remove construction, power, technology or tenant-concentration risk.

The less visible liability is larger than current bond calendars suggest. Goldman Sachs credit analysts led by Amanda Lynam estimated that hyperscalers have about $200 billion of recognized lease commitments and another $1 trillion of uncommenced leases disclosed in financial-statement footnotes. The latter figure rose from $725 billion in less than a month. Those contracts do not appear as lease liabilities until payments and use begin, but they represent future claims on cash flow and a pipeline of facilities that will need construction financing before occupancy.

Competition for capital is already affecting the upper end of credit. BNP Paribas found that CDS on high-quality European companies such as LVMH, Sanofi and BAE Systems had risen more than 10% since year-end even though those issuers have no direct data-center role. Global investment-grade bond spreads were around 80 basis points, only about 6 basis points above their post-financial-crisis low earlier this year. When hyperscalers issue at scale, tight-spread companies compete against larger, liquid alternatives and can converge toward index-level risk pricing without any deterioration in their own operations.

Broad credit returns on Thursday remained orderly. LQD's 0.41% gain exceeded the roughly 0.20%-0.23% advances in high-yield funds, consistent with the stronger duration rally in investment grade. Supplemental long-duration corporate indices rose about 0.64%-0.66%, close to the long Treasury index's 0.61% gain. Those total returns mainly show benchmark-yield relief and cannot identify cash-spread direction. Primary pricing and issuer terms provide the cleaner evidence that capital remains available but increasingly contested.

At the weaker end, access does not solve liability mismatch. Telesat took a $120 million term loan for general corporate purposes as its legacy geostationary-satellite business reported a 25% revenue decline and a C$12.7 million operating loss. It owes about $2.1 billion across four tranches over the next 14 months: a $1.32 billion term loan and $387 million senior-secured note mature in December, followed by a $225 million secured note next June and a $213 million unsecured note in October 2027. The company said current cash flow and reserves do not cover the obligations.

Telesat's corporate structure determines recovery risk. Last year's reorganization secured private loans against Telesat GEO but not the new low-Earth-orbit business, prompting an ongoing creditor lawsuit. Management expects to address the maturities and preserve GEO as a going concern, yet its filing identified substantial doubt over the December obligations. A 15-year Canadian military contract worth as much as C$2.7 billion including options and eligibility for $189 million from U.S. spectrum repurposing support the broader enterprise, but do not by themselves fund the near-term legacy maturities. The shares fell 13.4% Thursday.

Ukrainian Railways presents a different restructuring problem in which a realized revenue measure improves, but does not restore, creditor economics. A 30% freight-tariff increase took effect at the start of August after the company requested 45%. The state operator is preparing another proposal for $1.1 billion of bonds after talks failed in April. It stopped paying interest in January, and about $700 million matured last month without repayment; the balance is due in 2028. An additional 15% tariff increase proposed for January 2027 has not been approved.

The earlier plan contemplated a 20% principal reduction, a freight-volume adjustment mechanism, extension to 2033, amortization and higher coupons over time. Higher freight rates improve the cash-flow basis for renewed talks, but war damage, repair expense, energy and labor costs, lower freight volume and a structurally loss-making passenger business remain. Formal negotiations have not restarted. The relevant change is therefore an improved operating input, not a completed restructuring or restored payment record.

## Global Tightening Is Becoming More Local

Japan produced the clearest foreign-duration challenge to the U.S. rally. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's government was reported to support a near-term Bank of Japan increase, likely in September or October, as yen weakness and the fading effect of coordinated U.S.-Japan intervention aligned fiscal and monetary authorities. The 1% policy rate remains far below the Fed's 3.5%-3.75% range. Traders assigned a 74% probability to an increase at the BOJ's September 18 meeting, and Japan's 10-year yield edged up to 2.87%, near last month's three-decade high.

Fresh producer-price data strengthened the domestic case. Japanese corporate-goods prices rose 7.2% from a year earlier in July, only slightly below June's revised 7.3%, and increased 0.1% on the month after June was revised up to 0.5%. Oil, coal, chemicals and nonferrous metals led the annual pressure. Input-cost stress contributed to 556 inflation-related corporate bankruptcies in the first half, the highest since records began in 2018, followed by a monthly record of 121 in July. Yen weakness, energy and AI-related machinery demand all feed that pressure.

The currency response showed that one expected hike is not enough to resolve the rate differential. The yen briefly strengthened after the government signal but closed at 159.50 per dollar, its weakest close since July 30 and close to the 160 area that has previously drawn intervention. Market attention has shifted from whether the BOJ moves in September to the pace thereafter. Faster normalization may support the currency and retain domestic capital, but it also risks restraining an economy in which household spending fell for a seventh consecutive month in June.

Norway demonstrated a more balanced hold. Norges Bank kept its deposit rate at 4.25% for a second meeting, as all 16 surveyed analysts expected, and prepared no new forecasts. Governor Ida Wolden Bache said the committee needed more time after two benign core-inflation readings and that it was too early to conclude the outlook had materially changed. Officials still see wage growth and a tight labor market as sources of persistence, leaving another increase possible. Swaps priced 12 basis points by September and 22 basis points by year-end, down from 15 and 27 a day earlier.

Turkey's central bank remained restrictive for a different reason. Governor Fatih Karahan raised the year-end inflation forecast to 28% from 26%, closer to a 29% market survey, and acknowledged a partial failure to meet earlier projections. July inflation slowed to 31.8%, but energy uncertainty kept the bank funding at the 40% overnight rate instead of its suspended 37% one-week repo rate. The formal 2026 target remains 24%, and the new 2027 forecast and target are 15%. A return to one-week repo financing depends on future market conditions.

Vietnam shows how growth ambition can collide with the banking system's funding capacity. Dong loans exceed deposits by about 2 quadrillion dong, or $76.8 billion, according to the State Bank of Vietnam. The government seeks almost 12% growth in the second half and has urged lower lending rates, including preferential programs at least 1 percentage point below banks' average rates for comparable maturities. The central bank simultaneously warned that liquidity, domestic rates, the exchange rate and financial stability leave very limited room for monetary support.

The constraint is visible in both wholesale funding and inflation. Techcombank launched a $1 billion syndicated loan as banks sought offshore resources, while the SBV targets credit growth around 15% this year. July CPI was 4.45% year on year; holding average 2026 inflation near 4.5% would allow only about 0.34% average monthly increases through year-end. Vietnam therefore lacks the clean disinflationary latitude implied by the U.S. PPI. Credit expansion can support the government's growth goal, but an already negative deposit-loan gap raises the risk that lower administered lending costs migrate into liquidity and currency pressure.

These policy paths are not synchronized. U.S. data support waiting, Japan is aligning currency defense with earlier tightening, Norway is reassessing after downside inflation surprises, Turkey is maintaining de facto restraint after lifting its forecast, and Vietnam is trying to accelerate credit despite a funding gap. The common fixed-income consequence is competition among local curves and a wider range of policy outcomes. A Treasury rally based on U.S. producer prices can coexist with a high long-end premium when foreign investors face increasingly attractive or increasingly necessary yields at home.

## Forward Market Significance

The July core PCE release on August 26, the intervening employment reports and Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks determine whether Thursday's policy-sector rally becomes durable. A core PCE increase near the 0.2% projections derived from producer-price components, accompanied by continued hiring moderation and a chair willing to explain the July hold, would reinforce a September pause and keep the largest sensitivity in 2- to 5-year yields. Broad service inflation, stronger labor evidence or an emphasis on credibility after years above target would restore force to Hammack's dissent and reconnect the front end with the still-high real-rate regime.

The physical oil channel remains capable of overturning the disinflation interpretation. Sustained passage through the Strait of Hormuz, lower freight and insurance friction, and crude extending Thursday's decline would make July's falls in energy, food logistics and warehousing a more durable input to inflation. Renewed attacks, continued closure or another oil surge would make those readings backward-looking and test whether the 2-year yield and breakevens again rise together. The critical change is not another negotiating headline but a realized improvement or deterioration in physical flows before the next inflation and Fed decisions.

Japan and Indonesia provide the next foreign-duration tests on different horizons. Indonesia's August 14 budget speech needs a credible deficit path within the legal 3% ceiling, with a target below 2.5% and lower net issuance viewed as supportive; a 2.2% deficit could reduce projected 2027 net issuance to 722 trillion rupiah even as gross sales rise to 1.75 quadrillion rupiah. Japan's September 18 meeting must show whether government support, 7.2% producer inflation and a yen near 160 produce a hike and guidance for the path beyond it. Fiscal discipline in Indonesia and credible follow-through in Japan would strengthen local assets while raising the relative-value competition facing dollar duration; disappointment would redirect the pressure into their currencies and domestic long yields.
